title: One wearer, one week: beat-to-beat heart data from ordinary life, labelled as it happened
summary: 13 sessions, 17254 beats, 33 free-text notes typed while wearing the strap. Polar H10 chest strap, captured in a browser.

wearer.practice: daily yoga for years; also plays volleyball and tennis

device.capture: Web Bluetooth in Chrome, no vendor SDK

units.t_ms: integer milliseconds since the first beat of the session
units.rr_raw: RR interval in 1/1024 s, exactly as the strap reported it
units.rr_ms: not stored — it is rr_raw * 1000 / 1024, with no rounding
units.suspect: 1 where the beat failed the capture tool's plausibility check
units.seg: connection segment; beats either side of a dropout are not adjacent in time

how_to_load:
import json, pandas as pd
d = json.load(open('vagus-openset-v1.json'))
s = d['sessions'][0]
b = pd.DataFrame(s['beats'], columns=d['beat_columns'])
b['rr_ms'] = b.rr_raw * 1000 / 1024   # the only derivation
b['t_s']   = b.t_ms / 1000            # ms since session start
what_might_be_novel: Beat-to-beat RR from a chest strap in ordinary life — an office day, a drive through traffic, meditation, yoga — not a laboratory protocol and not wrist optics.
Thirty-three free-text notes typed by the wearer at the moment they felt something, each with a timestamp, so subjective state and physiology can be aligned rather than correlated after the fact.
A resonance sweep (4.5 to 6.5 breaths/min, two minutes each) in the same corpus as the free-breathing sessions, so a personal resonance rate can be located and then looked for in daily life.
Two cases where the physiology changed before the wearer wrote anything — by 28 seconds and by two minutes.
Recording quality is stated per session, not assumed: the suspect-beat fraction runs 0.0% to 2.1%, worst in the car.
limits: n = 1. One wearer, thirteen recordings, seven days. Nothing is replicated.
No control condition and no blinding. The wearer chose when to record and knew what was being tested.
Breathing rate is inferred from the heart, never measured at the chest. No breath has yet been counted against a clock in any of these recordings — this is the single cheapest missing validation.

Where the spectral peak and the count of the RR wave's own maxima disagree, breaths_per_min is null and the rejected estimate is kept beside it. That is thirteen of the twenty-eight measurable blocks.
Thirty of the thirty-three notes were typed while the strap was on. Three — all in the 17 Sep meeting — were corrected the next day from memory and carry retrospective = true.
swing_ms is the largest peak-to-trough excursion in the block, so longer blocks are flattered. median_swing_ms is given alongside and is the fairer comparison across unequal durations.
No medical claim of any kind. This is wellbeing and self-awareness data.
consent: Person-1 is the author of this dataset and consents to its publication. Three other wearers appear in the wider project and are deliberately excluded here: they agreed to personal use, not publication, and one of them is a minor.
license: CC BY 4.0 — use it, publish on it, say where it came from.
invitation: The findings in the demo are observations from one person, not results. If you can break them, or find something in these beats that the narration missed, that is the most useful thing that could happen to this project.

sessions.title: Morning baseline + sit
sessions.context: Morning, on waking. Before yoga and before coffee — a true fresh baseline. Protocol: 5 min seated rest (reading), 10 min free meditation, 4 min seated rest. Wearer reported being at about 50% energy, just up and not yet fully awake. The upward heart-rate drift across the session (63.5 -> 66.1) is most likely the waking curve rather than a response to the sitting.

labels.note: just out of meditation, things feel lighter and cleaner

sessions.title: After 20 minutes of yoga
sessions.context: Same morning, about 90 minutes after the pre-yoga baseline session (20260920T010623Z-44ee5a). Recorded immediately after 20 minutes of yoga. Wearer reported feeling light and relaxed, then light and energised with no tiredness. Some active discussion during the block. This is the 'after' half of a same-day before/after pair — test 14.

sessions.title: Sit cut short by an alarm
sessions.context: 06:47 IST, free meditation, about 10 minutes after the post-yoga rest and ~1.5 h after waking. Ended by an alarm at 11.2 min; the wearer's note: 'was just entering deeper meditation..then came out from alarm'. Three back-to-back flat episodes at 8.5, 8.8 and 9.1 min — about 50 seconds of near-flat heart in a row — precede that note by two minutes. Post-yoga, so heart-rate trend is confounded.
